slides.say: In the accompanying figure, the angles at A and C are equal. What is the value of m plus n over two?

The figure has three letters, k, m and n, but the answer has to be one number. So we'll write m and n with the same letter, k, and hope that k cancels. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with the angle rules, and then by plugging in a number for k.

[short pause] Start with m. m is outside the triangle at A, right next to the angle k inside. Together they make the straight line, so m and k add up to one hundred eighty. So m is one hundred eighty minus k.
at: So m is one hundred eighty

slides.say: Now n. n is outside the triangle at B, between side B C and the line of side A B that goes on past B. That's an exterior angle, and an exterior angle equals the two inside angles that are not next to it. Here they are the angles at A and at C, k and k. So n is k plus k, which is two k.
at: So n is k plus k

slides.say: Now the expression, m plus half of n. m is one hundred eighty minus k. Half of n is half of two k, which is k. So we get one hundred eighty minus k, plus k. Minus k and plus k cancel, and we're left with one hundred eighty. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way, plugging in a number. The answer is one number, so it comes out the same for every k that fits the figure. That means we're allowed to choose any k we like, and work with numbers instead of letters. Let's take an easy one, k is sixty.

Then the angles at A and C are sixty. The angle at B is one hundred eighty minus one hundred twenty, which is sixty too. m is next to the sixty at A, so m is one hundred eighty minus sixty, which is one hundred twenty. n is the outside angle at B, so n is sixty plus sixty, which is one hundred twenty too.
at: so m is one hundred eighty minus sixty
so n is sixty plus sixty
sixty, which is one hundred twenty too

slides.say: So m plus half of n is one hundred twenty plus sixty, which is one hundred eighty. Choice number three again. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
